originalTitle: Reliance Retail Q1 revenue rises, but profit falls as e-commerce weighs
simplifiedContent: Reliance Retail, a big retail company, had an 8.2% increase in sales in the first quarter of the year. However, the company's profit actually decreased by 14.2% because it spent a lot on its online shopping business, which affected its overall profitability. This means that even though the company is selling more, it's not making as much money as it used to. Reliance Consumer, a part of the company, did well with its sales more than doubling, especially with its grocery, electronics, and online commerce segments. This is important because it shows how the company is performing and how its investments in online shopping are impacting its bottom line.

originalTitle: JSW Steel’s profit doubles on revenue growth, beats estimates
simplifiedContent: JSW Steel, a steel company, made a lot of money in the April-June period, with its profit reaching Rs 4,696 crore, which is more than double what it made last year. This happened because the company's revenue (or sales) grew by about 10% and it was able to reduce its borrowing costs. The company's total expenses didn't increase much, which also helped its profit grow. This is good news for investors because the company's financial performance was better than expected. The company still plans to spend the same amount of money on new projects and investments as it had previously planned.

originalTitle: Netflix shares tumble over 10% as slowing growth, less viewership data spook investors
simplifiedContent: Netflix's stock price fell sharply, over 10%, because the company said it doesn't expect to make as much money as it thought it would. This worried investors, who are also concerned because Netflix will no longer share as much information about how many people are watching its shows. The company's forecast of slower growth, combined with less transparency about viewership, has made investors nervous about its future. This is a big deal because it caused the stock price to drop significantly from its previous high. The decline is partly due to a lackluster selection of new content released by Netflix this year.

originalTitle: Netflix shares tumble 13% after weak sales forecast, hit 22-month low
simplifiedContent: Netflix's stock price dropped 12.6% to its lowest point in almost two years. This happened because the company said it doesn't expect to make as much money as people thought it would, even though its recent financial results were okay. The company is having some problems with its original content and its stock price has been going down since the middle of 2025. As a result, Netflix is being more cautious about how much money it thinks it will make in 2026. This is important because it shows that the company's growth is slowing down, which is why investors are selling their shares and causing the price to drop.

originalTitle: Sebi clears automatic SWP, STP mandates for demat mutual fund holdings
simplifiedContent: The Indian stock market regulator, Sebi, has made a new rule for people who invest in mutual funds through a demat account. Before this rule, investors could only set up automatic instructions for mutual fund units held in a different form. Now, investors can set up automatic instructions, such as systematic withdrawal plans (SWP) and systematic transfer plans (STP), for mutual fund units held in their demat account. This means investors can easily transfer or withdraw money from their mutual fund investments without having to give new instructions every time. This change makes it more convenient for investors to manage their mutual fund investments.

originalTitle: Pulse of the Street: Earnings sentiment rescues volatile week; real test ahead
simplifiedContent: The Indian stock market had a volatile week, but it ended on a good note. The two main market indicators, the Sensex and the Nifty, both went up - the Sensex by 0.75% and the Nifty by 0.53% for the week. Most of these gains happened on Friday, with the Sensex rising 1.25% and the Nifty jumping 1.1%. This means that the market ended the week at a higher level than where it started. The Sensex even reached its highest closing level since June 12, 2026, which is a positive sign for investors.
